transit_depth_bls.name: transit_depth_bls
transit_depth_bls.label: Transit depth (BLS box)
transit_depth_bls.method: Box Least Squares best-fit box depth (no limb darkening; typically underestimates the true mid-transit depth).

transit_epoch.name: transit_epoch
transit_epoch.label: Transit epoch (mid-transit time)

uncertainty.interval: 68% (16th-84th percentile of covariance samples within physical bounds)

transit_epoch.method: Limb-darkened transit-model fit (reference transit nearest the data midpoint).

68% (16th-84th percentile of covariance samples within physical bounds)

radius_ratio.name: radius_ratio
radius_ratio.label: Radius ratio (Rp/R*)

uncertainty.interval: 68% (16th-84th percentile of covariance samples within physical bounds)

radius_ratio.method: Transit-model fit with quadratic limb darkening.

transit_snr.name: transit_snr
transit_snr.label: Transit signal-to-noise ratio
transit_snr.method: SNR = depth / (sigma_1 * beta) * sqrt(N_in): model depth over per-point noise inflated by the red-noise factor, times the square root of the number of in-transit points.

eccentricity.name: eccentricity
eccentricity.label: Eccentricity
eccentricity.method: Assumed circular; not constrained by transit photometry.

arg_periastron.name: arg_periastron
arg_periastron.label: Argument of periastron
arg_periastron.method: Undefined for a circular orbit; 90° makes all eccentricity factors unity.

stellar_mass.name: stellar_mass
stellar_mass.label: Stellar mass
stellar_mass.method: Newtonian gravity g = G M / R^2 with catalogue log g and radius.

stellar_luminosity.name: stellar_luminosity
stellar_luminosity.label: Stellar luminosity
stellar_luminosity.method: Stefan-Boltzmann law relative to the IAU nominal Sun.

stellar_density.name: stellar_density
stellar_density.label: Stellar density (from M*, R*)
stellar_density.method: Mean density from stellar mass and radius (Monte Carlo: mass and radius are correlated when the mass is derived from log g).

transit_depth.name: transit_depth
transit_depth.label: Transit depth (model, mid-transit)
transit_depth.method: Depth of the limb-darkened model at mid-transit (differs from k^2 by limb darkening and grazing geometry).
transit_depth.equation: delta = F_blocked(z = b; k, u1, u2)

transit_duration.name: transit_duration
transit_duration.label: Transit duration (T14)
transit_duration.method: First-to-fourth-contact duration of the fitted circular-orbit model (Winn 2010, eq. 14).
transit_duration.equation: T14 = P/pi asin( sqrt((1+k)^2 - b^2) / (a/R* sin i) )

transit_duration_full.name: transit_duration_full
transit_duration_full.label: Full-depth duration (T23)
transit_duration_full.equation: T23 = P/pi asin( sqrt((1-k)^2 - b^2) / (a/R* sin i) )

ingress_duration.name: ingress_duration
ingress_duration.label: Ingress/egress duration
ingress_duration.method: Half the difference between T14 and T23.

planet_radius.name: planet_radius
planet_radius.label: Planet radius
planet_radius.method: Rp = (Rp/R*) x R*, using the fitted radius ratio (not the sqrt(depth) approximation).
validation: Radius within the planetary regime (0.3-22.4 R⊕).

planet_mass.name: planet_mass
planet_mass.label: Planet mass
planet_mass.method: Chen & Kipping (2017) empirical mass-radius relation (Terran/Neptunian branches), including its intrinsic scatter. An estimate, not a measurement.
planet_mass.reason: Model estimate from radius only (Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relation, including its intrinsic scatter). No mass measurement is in the local KOI catalogue (the NASA Exoplanet Archive was not queried). A radial-velocity or transit-timing mass measurement would make the mass, and the bulk density, surface gravity and escape velocity derived from it, measurements. Relative uncertainty exceeds 30%.

semi_major_axis.name: semi_major_axis
semi_major_axis.label: Semi-major axis
semi_major_axis.method: Kepler's third law with the stellar mass (planet mass neglected).

inclination.name: inclination
inclination.label: Orbital inclination
inclination.method: From the impact parameter and scaled semi-major axis (Winn 2010, eq. 7).
inclination.equation: cos i = (b R*/a) (1 + e sin w) / (1 - e^2)

stellar_density_transit.name: stellar_density_transit
stellar_density_transit.label: Stellar density (transit-derived)
stellar_density_transit.reason: Not constrained by the light curve alone: the ingress (5.22 +0.72 / −0.44 min) is shorter than half the 29.4-minute exposure, so the transit shape cannot separate the impact parameter from a/R*. Shorter-cadence photometry (e.g. Kepler 1-minute data) is needed for an independent stellar density.

orbital_velocity.name: orbital_velocity
orbital_velocity.label: Mean orbital velocity
orbital_velocity.method: Mean orbital speed 2 pi a / P.

insolation.name: insolation
insolation.label: Stellar insolation
insolation.method: Orbit-averaged incident flux relative to Earth.

equilibrium_temperature.name: equilibrium_temperature
equilibrium_temperature.label: Equilibrium temperature

systematic: Bond albedo and heat redistribution are assumed (see systematic_range).

equilibrium_temperature.method: Radiative equilibrium with assumed Bond albedo 0.3 and 'full' heat redistribution.

systematic_range.basis: Bond albedo 0-0.7 and full vs dayside-only heat redistribution (central inputs). Not included in the statistical interval.

hz_inner_conservative.name: hz_inner_conservative
hz_inner_conservative.label: HZ inner edge (conservative)
hz_inner_conservative.method: Kopparapu et al. (2014) 'runaway greenhouse' boundary, d = sqrt(L*/S_eff).
hz_inner_conservative.equation: S_eff = S0 + aT + bT^2 + cT^3 + dT^4, T = Teff - 5780 K

hz_outer_conservative.name: hz_outer_conservative
hz_outer_conservative.label: HZ outer edge (conservative)
hz_outer_conservative.method: Kopparapu et al. (2014) 'maximum greenhouse' boundary, d = sqrt(L*/S_eff).
hz_outer_conservative.equation: S_eff = S0 + aT + bT^2 + cT^3 + dT^4, T = Teff - 5780 K

hz_inner_optimistic.name: hz_inner_optimistic
hz_inner_optimistic.label: HZ inner edge (optimistic)
hz_inner_optimistic.method: Kopparapu et al. (2014) 'recent venus' boundary, d = sqrt(L*/S_eff).
hz_inner_optimistic.equation: S_eff = S0 + aT + bT^2 + cT^3 + dT^4, T = Teff - 5780 K

hz_outer_optimistic.name: hz_outer_optimistic
hz_outer_optimistic.label: HZ outer edge (optimistic)
hz_outer_optimistic.method: Kopparapu et al. (2014) 'early mars' boundary, d = sqrt(L*/S_eff).
hz_outer_optimistic.equation: S_eff = S0 + aT + bT^2 + cT^3 + dT^4, T = Teff - 5780 K

planet_density.name: planet_density
planet_density.label: Planet bulk density
planet_density.method: Bulk density from mass and radius.
planet_density.reason: Uses the model-estimated planet mass (Chen & Kipping 2017), not a measured one. The mass contributes 83% of its uncertainty and the radius 17%. (Mass and radius are correlated, r = 0.27, because the mass is computed from the radius; the reported interval includes that correlation, the split above does not.) Relative uncertainty exceeds 30%. A measured mass would make it a measurement.

planet_surface_gravity.name: planet_surface_gravity
planet_surface_gravity.label: Surface gravity
planet_surface_gravity.method: Surface gravity from mass and radius.
planet_surface_gravity.reason: Uses the model-estimated planet mass (Chen & Kipping 2017), not a measured one. The mass contributes 92% of its uncertainty and the radius 8%. (Mass and radius are correlated, r = 0.27, because the mass is computed from the radius; the reported interval includes that correlation, the split above does not.) Relative uncertainty exceeds 30%. A measured mass would make it a measurement.

escape_velocity.name: escape_velocity
escape_velocity.label: Escape velocity
escape_velocity.method: Escape velocity from mass and radius.
escape_velocity.reason: Uses the model-estimated planet mass (Chen & Kipping 2017), not a measured one. The mass contributes 98% of its uncertainty and the radius 2%. (Mass and radius are correlated, r = 0.27, because the mass is computed from the radius; the reported interval includes that correlation, the split above does not.) Relative uncertainty exceeds 30%. A measured mass would make it a measurement.

classifications.name: size_category
classifications.label: Planet size category
classifications.basis: Planet-radius bins of Borucki et al. (2011, ApJ 736, 19), as used for Kepler candidate statistics.
caveats: Based on radius alone; says nothing about mass or composition.

classifications.name: composition_candidate
classifications.label: Radius-based composition candidate
classifications.basis: Radius-only composition candidates: most planets larger than ~1.6 R_earth are not purely rocky (Rogers 2015, ApJ 801, 41); the radius valley near 1.5-2 R_earth separates rocky super-Earths from volatile-rich sub-Neptunes (Fulton et al. 2017, AJ 154, 109); ~10 R_earth marks the transition to gas giants.
caveats: Planetary mass is not measured, so bulk composition cannot be determined: planets of the same radius span a wide range of densities. This label is a radius-based candidate category only.
Atmospheric and interior composition are not inferred.

classifications.name: irradiation
classifications.label: Relative stellar irradiation
classifications.basis: Descriptive bins of incident flux relative to Earth (S_earth = 1). Not a standard taxonomy.
caveats: Orbit-averaged incident flux; does not account for atmospheric response.

classifications.name: thermal_regime
classifications.label: Approximate thermal regime
classifications.basis: Descriptive equilibrium-temperature regimes; 'ultra-hot' follows the ~2000-2200 K threshold used for ultra-hot Jupiters (Parmentier et al. 2018). Teq is not a surface temperature.
caveats: Equilibrium temperature depends on the assumed Bond albedo and heat redistribution; it is not a surface temperature (greenhouse warming, internal heat and clouds are not modelled).

classifications.name: habitable_zone
classifications.label: Estimated habitable-zone position
classifications.category: Interior to the habitable zone (too irradiated)
classifications.basis: Kopparapu et al. (2014, ApJL 787, L29) habitable-zone flux boundaries for a 1 M_earth planet, valid for 2600-7200 K host stars; compares the planet's orbit-averaged insolation with the boundary fluxes for the host star's effective temperature.
caveats: An estimated habitable-zone position is not evidence of habitability or of life: it ignores the planet's mass, atmosphere, composition and climate.
Boundaries are model-dependent and computed for a 1 M_earth planet.

limb_darkening.note: Representative Kepler-band coefficients for a Sun-like dwarf; not fitted.

folded.note: Detrended transit windows folded on the fitted ephemeris and binned; the model is the best-fit limb-darkened transit. For display only.

transit_fit.method: Bounded least-squares fit of a quadratic-limb-darkened circular-orbit transit model to locally detrended windows around each transit; covariance from the Jacobian, inflated by reduced chi^2 and the red-noise factor beta.
transit_fit.bls_note: The transit-search (BLS) SNR is the box-depth signal-to-noise ratio, depth / (sigma sqrt(1/N_in + 1/N_out)), assuming white noise. The model-fit SNR above uses the fitted limb-darkened mid-transit depth (deeper than the box average) and inflates the noise by the red-noise factor beta, so the two differ; neither is a probability.

transit_timing.assessment: Transit times are consistent with a linear ephemeris (chi^2 = 4.2 for 9 dof, p = 0.90); no significant timing variations.

consistency_checks.label: Transit-derived vs catalogue stellar density
consistency_checks.note: Not evaluated: the light curve alone does not bound the stellar density at this SNR/cadence (ingress 5.22 +0.72 / −0.44 min is shorter than half the 29.4-min exposure, so the transit shape is not resolved), so no independent comparison with the catalogue is possible. The catalogue density is neither confirmed nor contradicted.

consistency_checks.label: Linear-ephemeris vs global-fit period
consistency_checks.note: Period from individually timed transits compared with the global fit.

catalog_comparison.label: Transit depth (model, mid-transit)
catalog_comparison.note: Catalogue depth is from NASA's own transit fit; the BLS-seeded fit here is independent.

catalog_comparison.label: Equilibrium temperature
catalog_comparison.note: NASA koi_teq assumes Bond albedo 0.3 and full redistribution.

assumptions.text: Star and planet radiate as blackbodies; no internal heat or greenhouse effect.
Bond albedo A = 0.3 (assumed; the NASA KOI table convention is 0.3). Albedo is not measured from the light curve.
Stellar Teff, log g and radius from the local NASA Exoplanet Archive KOI cumulative table (Kepler DR25 stellar properties).
Circular orbit (e = 0) unless an eccentricity is supplied by expert override. Transit photometry alone does not constrain eccentricity, so this is an assumption, not a result.
Planet mass estimated from radius with the Chen & Kipping (2017) empirical mass-radius relation, including its intrinsic scatter. An estimate, not a measurement.
Transit-fit uncertainties from the linearised covariance at the best fit (Gaussian approximation), sampled with physical bounds enforced.
Heat redistribution 'full' (f = 0.25 in Teq = Teff sqrt(R*/a) [f(1-A)]^1/4).
Habitable-zone boundaries from Kopparapu et al. (2014) for a 1 M_earth planet.
Quadratic limb darkening fixed at u1 = 0.40, u2 = 0.26 (representative Kepler-band values for a Sun-like dwarf); not fitted.
Planet mass neglected in Kepler's third law unless a measured mass is supplied.
No third-light dilution: the measured depth is assumed to come from the target star alone.

The transit fit uses the catalogue stellar density (from log g and R*) as a Gaussian prior on a/R*, which breaks the impact-parameter / a/R* degeneracy. This assumes a circular orbit and accurate catalogue stellar parameters; the prior-free fit is kept for the transit-vs-catalogue density check.
The uploaded time column is in days; no barycentric correction or BJD offset is applied.
Photometric uncertainties estimated empirically from out-of-transit point-to-point scatter, inflated by the measured red-noise factor.
